# Machine learning {#sec-machine-learning}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Fundamental knowledge about machine learning. How machine learning is used
in bioinformatics. Recent progress in machine learning methodologies.
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction: supervised vs. unsupervised learning; classic models
used in bioinformatics (HMMs, neural networks, SVMs, random forests); how
to train and evaluate without fooling yourself (homology-aware splits,
overfitting); deep learning architectures (CNNs, RNNs, transformers,
diffusion) and protein/DNA language models.
:::

## Key concepts

- Supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning; classification vs. regression
- Hidden Markov models: Viterbi, forward–backward, Baum–Welch; applications (gene finding, profiles, TM topology)
- Artificial neural networks: perceptron, backpropagation, gradient descent
- Support vector machines, kernels; decision trees and random forests
- Generalisation: overfitting, regularisation, cross-validation, train/validation/test splits
- Bioinformatics pitfalls: homology between training and test sets (redundancy reduction), data leakage, class imbalance
- Evaluation: accuracy, precision/recall, ROC and PR curves, MCC; benchmarking (CASP, CAFA)
- Deep learning: convolutional and recurrent networks, attention and transformers, graph neural networks, diffusion models
- Language models for proteins and DNA (ESM, embeddings); transfer learning
- Interpretability and reporting standards (DOME)

## Key papers

::: {.callout-tip}
★ = the 2021 version of the exam was based on @sapoval2022 together with
@pevsner2015.
:::

### Reviews — start here

- ★ @sapoval2022 — current progress and open challenges for deep learning across the biosciences.
- @greener2022 — a guide to machine learning for biologists.
- @tarca2007 — machine learning and its applications to biology.
- @lecun2015 — deep learning.
- @ching2018 — opportunities and obstacles for deep learning in biology and medicine.
- @eraslan2019 — deep learning for genomics.

### Short primers (Nature Biotechnology "What is…?" / Points of Significance)

- @eddy2004 — what is a hidden Markov model?
- @krogh2008 — what are artificial neural networks?
- @noble2006 — what is a support vector machine?
- @lever2016 — model selection and overfitting.

### Classic

- @rabiner1989 — a tutorial on hidden Markov models.
- @krogh1994 — HMMs in computational biology.
- @rost1993 — profiles + neural networks for secondary structure.

### Good practice

- @jones2019 — setting the standards for machine learning in biology.
- @walsh2021 — DOME: recommendations for supervised machine learning validation in biology.

### Modern architectures and applications

- @vaswani2017 — attention is all you need (transformers).
- @rives2021 — protein language models (ESM).
- @jumper2021 — AlphaFold2 (see @sec-protein-structure).
- @avsec2021 — Enformer: gene expression from sequence with long-range interactions.

### Textbooks

- @hastie2009 — *The Elements of Statistical Learning* (free PDF).
- @durbin1998 — *Biological Sequence Analysis* (HMMs and probabilistic models).
